children: The Indian equity market is likely to open cautiously on Wednesday despite positive global cues. As foreign portfolio investors stepped in to sell, analysts expect the market to remain under pressure.

Continued foreign outflows and elevated global bond yields remained an overhang for domestic equities, said Ajit Mishra, SVP – research, Religare Broking. On Tuesday, FPIs offloaded shares worth Rs3,810 crore.

The Derivatives structure has also turned cautious. Put-call ratio stands at 0.99, with total Call OI of 14.53 crore contracts against Put OI of 12.99 crore. “Call concentration around 23,400–23,500 is likely to act as immediate overhead supply, with further Call OI visible towards 23,700–24,000. Put positioning around 23,300 and 23,100 provides downside cushioning, making 23,300–23,270 an important demand zone.,” said Dhupesh Dhameja, Derivatives Research Analyst, SAMCO Securities

Meanwhile, India VIX declined 2.12% to 10.99, keeping volatility subdued despite the index weakness. “This suggests that the decline is currently controlled rather than indicative of a broad volatility expansion,” he added.

Overall, the near-term bias remains cautious below 23,430. Sustained buying above 23,500 can revive the recovery towards 23,670, whereas a decisive break below 23,270 would increase downside risk towards 23,060.
Most Asian stocks are closed for the holiday today.

The index on the daily chart formed a bearish candle, signalling selling pressure at higher levels, as Nifty snapped its 4-sessionup move and closed lower around 23,350. The index has been consolidating over the last 5 sessions, with last Tuesday’s sizable bearish candle highlighting consolidation after the recent sharp decline.
Nifty likely to remain in consolidation
Technically, the market remains under consolidation, analysts said.

Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking, said Nifty is likely to extend its recent consolidation and trade in the broad range of 23,115-23,650 in the coming sessions. On the upside, 23,600-23,650 will act as major resistance, as it is the last week high and the recent breakdown area. The index needs to sustain a higher-high, higher-low formation and reclaim 23,650 to signal a pause in the ongoing downtrend.

title: Nifty may remain under pressure as FPI selling continues; key levels to watch
